newsitem.title: USA: Texaco may seek French refining, marketing partner.
newsitem.headline: Texaco may seek French refining, marketing partner.

text.p: Texaco Inc. may seek a French partner to shore up its struggling European refining and marketing business, analysts said Wednesday, and the betting is that it will be the big French oil company, Total SA.
Texaco owns one refinery in Europe, a 180,000 barrel-a-day plant in Britain, and has a 35 percent stake in another. Its petroleum product sales last year were 461,000 barrels a day.
Analysts estimate Texaco has 7 percent of the British gasoline market and a somewhat smaller share in Europe.

Making and selling gasoline and other refined products is not very profitable for oil companies, in the United States or in Europe, where the situation is worse because of price wars in Britain and France.
Texaco Chief Executive Peter Bijur told industry analysts in February that the company would complete a study in 90 days on its European options, and that time is now up.
"When I talked to them a few days ago, they said nothing had been decided, but after the BP and Mobil success, it is just a question of time," said one New York-based analyst.
British Petroleum Co. Plc and Mobil Corp. have estimated their European refining and marketing venture would generate benefits of $400 million to $500 million, before taxes.
A spokesman for Texaco said that there were no specific partners under consideration at the moment, but added that the company was looking hard at its European refining business.
Operating earnings at Texaco's international refining and marketing fell to $252 million in 1996 from $358 million in 1995, due to weakness in the British market.

Analysts said Texaco believes that it is big enough not to have to form a downstream venture with another major U.S. oil company such as Exxon Corp. or Texaco's existing U.S. downstream partner Royal Dutch/Shell.
And BP is off-limits because of its deal with Mobil.
"Among the European majors, that leaves France's Total SA or Elf Aquitaine, with Total the more likely," one analyst said.
Further credence is being given to a Total deal by traders of the French oil giant's American Depositary Receipts.
"We hear Total may announce a restructuring as early as this week," said one trader, noting the company did not say anything at its shareholder meeting Wednesday.
European analysts said one possibility in Europe was a series of smaller alliances.
"People may be looking at deals on a regional basis, although something people have talked about is a possible link-up between Elf and Total," said Greg Quine at J.P. Morgan in London.
Elf already has a British venture with Chevron Corp. This deal will actually result in the much needed closure of European refining capacity at Chevron's Gulf Oil unit.
However, big closures as a result of mergers are as unlikely in Europe as they are here because companies face charges against earnings and environmental costs.
Total Chairman Thierry Desmarest has said he would like to see a deal based on cutting refining capacity in Europe, but analysts are sceptical that this will happen.
Instead Desmarest is cutting spending on refineries to the bone and the company has slashed its French retail locations 11 percent to 3,300 between 1993 and 1995.
"The industry here is very tight and the base position is that everyone is talking to everyone else in Europe as in the U.S.," said Morgan's Quine.
